text.p: Latvia's Ventspil's Nafta oil terminal said on Monday that the volumes of oil and oil products it will handle in 1997 would be around the same level as the 25.3 million tonnes handled in 1996.
Ventspils, on the government's privatisation list, made an unaudited profit in 1996 of 34 million lats versus 19.5 million lats in 1995, the company added.
"We plan the same volumes as last year, around 20 million to 25 million tonnes," Ventspils Nafta president Janis Blazhevich told journalists.

"We are having good progress in throughput already this year and we will have more but not much because the railway will not be able to supply us more and the pipeline is working close to its maximum," Blazhevich added.
Oil and oil products arrive at Ventspils via pipeline from Samara in Russia and via railway.
The company in the first quarter of this year reloaded some 6.7 million tonnes of oil and oil products, some 600,000 tonnes more than in the same period of 1996.
Blazhevich said that the privatisation plans recently announced for Ventspils Nafta did not have a big role for foreign strategic investors, including those from Russia.
The privatisation agency recently announced it would sell Ventspils in four stages, with just seven percent of its stock to be offered for sale abroad.
Some 15.5 percent will be sold in a public offer and the state will finally be left with 26 percent of the shares.
"Where do we have strategic investors and Russian companies in this plan, that has not been answered," Blazhevich said.
He said the privatisation plan was more concerned with the interests of Latvian companies and people, who can take part in the selloff via privatisation vouchers.

"The aim of the current programme most probably is to have a strategic investor when the company (Ventspils) needs money or when it has a specific project. At the moment, Ventspils Nafta does not need any money," he said.
Blazhevich also said that the previously announced project to deepen the waters of the port to allow it to take bigger tankers would be completed around the end of this year.
